status.label: Reproduce mixed-DPI zone geometry
status.detail: The constant-size gap and application-specific behavior need requested-versus-visible-frame measurements.

next_action.label: Compare DPI-aware and unaware window frames
next_action.reason: Do not assume a simple scale-factor error when the reported gap is roughly constant.

judgment.rationale: The report supplies mixed-DPI scaling transitions, affected applications, screenshots and multiple archives. Later observations include a roughly 16-pixel gap at widely different scale factors and a spacing-minus-one result.
evidence: PowerToys 0.64/0.66/0.80 reports Paint, Notepad++, VBA and other windows changing size/gap when another monitor's scaling changes.
The public discussion already contains three diagnostic archives and describes 125% versus 350% scaling with a similar gap.
FancyZones WindowUtils.cpp checks window DPI awareness and mixed monitor scaling, with special frame-adjustment/clipping logic.
No concrete linked implementation establishes a fix for the reported application and scaling-transition matrix.
judgment.recommended_action: Measure requested zone rect, actual window rect and DWM extended frame before/after scaling changes on the affected applications.

fix_assessment.rationale: A source-grounded mixed-DPI/frame-adjustment investigation is appropriate; the exact correction is not established by screenshots alone.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep zone placement consistent through mixed-DPI frame changes
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: DPI-awareness-dependent frame adjustment or a stale adjustment during display scaling produces the gap. A constant offset rather than proportional scaling argues against asserting a generic missing DPI multiplication.
plan: Reproduce the report with a mixed-DPI pair and record application DPI awareness, requested zone rect, GetWindowRect and DWM extended-frame bounds.
Compare scaling set before launch against live scaling changes, with zero, positive and reported negative spacing controls.
Trace WindowUtils adjustment/clipping and coordinate conversions to the first incorrect rectangle; change only that confirmed conversion or invalidation boundary.
Add regression coverage for unaffected per-monitor-aware windows, unaware/system-aware windows and same-DPI monitors.
verification: Visible window frames align with the configured zone after live scale changes.
125% and 350% controls do not develop a constant unintended gap.
Intentional spacing and normal resizable/maximized window handling remain unchanged.

confidence.rationale: The report's scaling/application matrix and inspected mixed-DPI frame branches identify a concrete investigation boundary; actual rectangle measurements are needed to choose a correction.

issue_context.summary: FancyZones can leave application-specific gaps or size changes when scaling differs between monitors or changes during a session.
known_information: The report names affected applications and multiple releases and supplies screenshots and three archives.
The gap is described as roughly constant across very different scaling factors.
FancyZones has DPI-awareness and mixed-monitor-specific adjustment code.
inferences: Frame-border adjustment or stale coordinate state is plausible; the evidence does not justify a single blanket scale-factor fix.
issue_context.analysis: The existing settings and attachments are sufficient to build a maintainer geometry matrix. Another generic diagnostic request would not substitute for comparing requested and visible rectangles.
initial_investigation: Read the complete report and discussion, including negative-spacing and constant-gap observations.
Inspected WindowUtils mixed-DPI and window-awareness adjustment logic.
Checked obvious linked work without finding an exact verified fix.

actions.label: Review mixed-DPI geometry plan
actions.description: Approve a measured rectangle investigation before selecting a frame/conversion change.

prerequisites: Use two monitors with independently configurable scaling and record topology/Windows/PowerToys versions.
Use the affected application versions where available and an instrumented FancyZones build; identify each window's actual DPI-awareness context.
steps: Apply a zero-spacing layout and snap an affected window; record zone, window and extended-frame rectangles.
Change the other monitor from 125% to a substantially different scaling value, including 350% if supported, and snap again.
Repeat with scaling configured before application launch and with a per-monitor-aware control application.
Repeat configured positive and negative spacing, preserving the distinction between intentional spacing and unintended frame gaps.
reproduce.expected_result: Actual visible frames follow the intended zone/spacing without stale mixed-DPI offsets.
reproduce.setup_prompt: Prepare a mixed-DPI two-monitor geometry test with affected applications and a per-monitor-aware control. Capture only rectangle coordinates, awareness contexts and scale factors; no personal window content is required.
